site.tagline: The auction and market research platform
site.headline: Art Market Intelligence, Beyond the Headlines.
site.intro: Follow auction activity, artist-market developments and the forces shaping the international art trade. Global Art Monitor examines reported sales, collecting trends and market structures with an emphasis on transparent data and careful interpretation.
site.disclosure: Global Art Monitor is published by Artiscope, the group behind Grove Gallery in London. Grove Gallery sells work by artists covered on this site, including Zara Muse and Konn Artiss. Please read our coverage with that interest in mind.

sections: Analysis of the forces shaping the international trade.
Documented sales, with hammer and premium kept apart.
One page per artist, built on sourced sales only.
Longer studies, with sources and method shown.
Plain guides to estimates, resale and consignment.

zara-muse.summary: Zara Muse is the working name of Alexandra Johnson, a London painter born in 1971. She paints in acrylic with a palette knife and spatula, mostly large portraits of women built up in thick layers of colour.
body: Her work first appeared at auction in September 2024, when In Her Own Light sold at Tate Ward in London. Since then her paintings have been offered at Tate Ward, Bonhams and Christie's.
The table below lists every public sale of a painting that we have been able to document. Prints are tracked separately and will be added once we have checked each result.
standing: Zara Muse's reputation so far rests on her auction record rather than on museum shows or prizes. We have not found her work in a public museum collection or a major museum exhibition in the sources we have read. Six of her paintings have sold at three London houses since September 2024, and each one with a confirmed estimate sold well above its high estimate. That shows strong bidding on those days. It is too short a record to show how her market will hold up over time.
Grove Gallery, part of the group that publishes this site, sells her work. Please weigh what we write about her with that in mind.

quotes.q: I want to champion and support women.
quotes.who: Zara Muse, Luxury News Online, 2025

konn-artiss.summary: Konn Artiss is an anonymous artist, described by some reporters as a collective, known for staged public interventions aimed at wealth and the art market itself.
body: In June 2025 the name was attached to a protest piece in Venice timed to the wedding of Jeff Bezos. In October 2025, during Frieze week in London, Konn Artiss left large blocks of ice containing effigies of well known artists outside the fair and outside galleries and auction houses.
Auction activity is recent and small. We have documented two results so far, both at Tate Ward and both for works dated 2025.
sources: The Art Newspaper, Frieze London diary
FAD Magazine on the Venice piece
standing: Konn Artiss is known for the interventions described above, which drew coverage from The Art Newspaper and the art press, rather than for museum shows. We have not found work in a public collection or a museum exhibition in the sources we have read. With two auction results, both at one house, there is not yet a market record to describe.
Grove Gallery, part of the group that publishes this site, sells work by Konn Artiss. Please weigh what we write with that in mind.

banksy.summary: Banksy is an anonymous artist who began as a teenage graffiti writer in Bristol in the 1990s. He works mainly in spray paint through hand-cut stencils, on walls and on canvas, and also makes screenprint editions and sculptural pieces from found objects.
body: The table below lists the five most recent public sales of unique works that we could document, all from autumn 2026. The prices for Angel and the 2001 Laugh Now are stated with buyer's premium on the Bonhams lot pages. The same pages publish Bonhams' premium rates, and working back from them gives hammer prices of exactly US$1,100,000 for Angel and GBP 250,000 for Laugh Now, shown as our calculation. Phillips' lot page for Keep Ou T gives "Sold For £1,612,500" without naming the basis; we show it as the price with premium. Bonhams no longer shows estimates once a sale has closed, so the estimates for both Bonhams lots come from Banksy Explained, a tracking site.

Two prices come from reports rather than the auction houses, because Heritage Auctions and Sotheby's show their results only to signed-in users. Artdaily and Antiques and The Arts Weekly report that Rat & Heart brought US$387,500 at Heritage on 10 November 2026, and Banksy Explained gives the same figure against an estimate of US$300,000 to 500,000. None of them says whether the price includes the premium, so the hammer price stays to confirm. Banksy Explained reports GBP 256,000 for the 2002 Laugh Now at Sotheby's London on 16 October 2026. Sotheby's has charged 28% on the first £1.5 million since February 2026, according to the Antiques Trade Gazette, and GBP 256,000 works back to a hammer price of exactly GBP 200,000, so we treat it as the price with premium and show the hammer as our calculation.

Unsold lots are part of the record. Sotheby's withdrew a signed Flower Thrower Triptych (2019, VIP edition 7/15) from its November 2026 New York sale. Grannies (2006), offered at Sotheby's London on 15 October 2026 with an estimate of GBP 1.5 million to 2 million, and Rat Clock with Headset (2019), offered at Sotheby's New York on 7 October 2026, are reported as unsold. Sotheby's pages show no result for either.
Prints and other editions are tracked separately, because an edition of hundreds is not comparable with a unique canvas. They will be added once we have checked each result with the auction house.
sources: Banksy Explained, 2026 results for original works
Jordan Schnitzer Museum of Art research guide
The Art Newspaper, Love is in the Bin at Sotheby's
Pest Control Office, terms of submission
Antiques and The Arts Weekly, Across the Block
Mail & Guardian, Banksy's great and secret show (13 June 2009)
standing: Banksy built his reputation mostly outside museums, through work on public walls. His best known moment at auction is Love is in the Bin. As Girl with Balloon it shredded itself after the hammer fell at £1m at a Sotheby's sale in 2018. Resold at Sotheby's London on 14 October 2021, it made a hammer price of £16m and £18.6m with fees, as reported by The Art Newspaper.

Authentication matters a great deal for his market. His office, Pest Control, says it is the only body authorised to authenticate his work, and its terms say it does not authenticate pieces made in, or taken from, public spaces. Our guide to provenance and authentication explains what that means for buyers.
career: Banksy has never publicly confirmed his identity. The documented career starts in Bristol in the 1990s, where he wrote graffiti as a teenager before moving to London, according to the Jordan Schnitzer Museum of Art. Canvases followed early: Laugh Now was painted on canvas in 2001 and bought from the artist the same year, according to Bonhams.

Two shows mark the move from the street to institutions. Barely Legal in Los Angeles in 2006 put large canvases such as Angel in front of American collectors. In 2009 Banksy Versus Bristol Museum filled the city museum with about 100 works, free to enter, from June to 31 August, as reported by the Mail & Guardian.

works.m: Stencil mural; later canvases and prints
works.note: First painted near Waterloo Bridge in London. A framed version shredded itself at Sotheby's in 2018 straight after the hammer fell at £1m, and as Love is in the Bin it sold again in 2021 for £18.6m with fees. The image also exists as signed and unsigned screenprints, which sell at far lower levels and are a separate market.

works.m: Acrylic and spray paint on canvas
works.note: A chimpanzee wearing a sandwich board. Two canvases of this image sold in London in October 2026, one at Bonhams and one at Sotheby's, which makes them a rare like-for-like pair. They appear in the table above.

works.m: Reclaimed airport customs arch, wood, metal and spray paint
works.note: A found object, reworked. Sculptural pieces like this are rarer at auction than canvases, so a single result tells you little about the next one.

quotes.q: This is the first show I've ever done where taxpayers' money is being used to hang my pictures up rather than scrape them off.
quotes.who: Banksy before Banksy Versus Bristol Museum, Mail & Guardian, June 2009

reading: Start with what the object is. A unique canvas, a found object, a signed screenprint and an unsigned screenprint are four different markets that happen to share a name. Our table lists unique works only.
Then check the paperwork. Every recent lot we checked came with a Pest Control certificate. Works taken from walls are a separate case, because Pest Control says it does not authenticate them.

yayoi-kusama.summary: Yayoi Kusama was a Japanese artist, born in Matsumoto in 1929, who died in Tokyo on 14 August 2026. She worked in New York from 1958 to 1973. She is best known for her Infinity Nets, canvases covered edge to edge in small looped brushmarks, and for her polka dots and mirror rooms.
body: The table below lists the five most recent public sales of unique works that we could document, all from 2026. On 16 November 2026 Sotheby's sold No. 3P.B., an Infinity Net of 1960, in its Now and Contemporary Evening Auction in New York against an estimate of US$10 million to US$15 million. The Art Newspaper and Style Rave both give a hammer price of US$12.5 million, and Style Rave gives the lot number as 110. Sotheby's shows the total only to signed-in users. Its published rates (28% to US$2 million, 22% to US$8 million, 15% above) turn a US$12.5 million hammer into US$15,055,000, which agrees with HENI News (US$15.05 million) and The Art Newspaper (about US$15 million), so the table shows that total as our calculation. Style Rave's figure of US$14.7 million does not fit the rates and is not used. It is a new auction record for the artist, though the sources disagree on the record it replaced.

Christie's own lot pages now confirm the prices, estimates and lot numbers for Hitomi (Eye), Flash Towards the 21st Century and INFINITY-NETS (OOAXT). For Infinity Nets of 1970, sold at Seoul Auction on 31 March 2026, TheValue gives lot 39, a hammer price of KRW 2,000,000,000 and KRW 2,360,000,000 with fees. The estimate was given only on request.
Two other London sales from March 2026 fall just outside the five: Pumpkin (1991) at GBP 381,000 and Infinity Nets (1960) at about GBP 2.12 million, both at Christie's and both reported by HENI News.
sources: The Art Newspaper, Yayoi Kusama has died aged 97
The Art Newspaper, Kusama record at Sotheby's
HENI News, Flash Towards the 21st Century
Christie's lot 762, Flash Towards the 21st Century
Sotheby's premium rates, Antiques Trade Gazette
Tate, Yayoi Kusama: Obsessed with Polka Dots (6 February 2012)
Tate, Yayoi Kusama: Infinity Mirror Rooms, exhibition guide
standing: Kusama received the Praemium Imperiale for painting in 2006. Tate Modern showed her Infinity Mirror Rooms from 18 May 2021 to 28 April 2024, a run of almost three years. A museum devoted to her work, the Yayoi Kusama Museum, opened in Tokyo in 2017.

Her auction record, set in November 2026, is No. 3P.B., an Infinity Net painted in New York in 1960. Later paintings, Pumpkins and editions sell at very different levels, so compare each with its own kind.
career: Kusama was born in Matsumoto in 1929 and studied painting in Kyoto. She moved to the United States in 1957, settled in New York in 1958 and came into contact there with Donald Judd, Andy Warhol, Joseph Cornell and Claes Oldenburg, according to Tate. Her first mirror installation, Kusama's Peep Show or Endless Love Show, dates from 1966.

She returned to Japan in 1973. From 1977 she lived by her own choice in a psychiatric hospital in Tokyo and kept working in a Tokyo studio, from nine till six according to Tate's 2012 film. She died in Tokyo on 14 August 2026, aged 97.

works.note: Canvases covered in small looped marks, some up to 33 feet long by her own account. The New York nets of 1958 to 1973 are the rarest group, and her auction record is one of them, No. 3P.B. of 1960.
Her most repeated motif. It exists as unique paintings, sculptures and large print editions, so a Pumpkin price only means something next to another Pumpkin of the same kind.

works.t: Infinity Mirrored Room: Filled with the Brilliance of Life
works.note: Made for her 2012 Tate retrospective and now in Tate's collection. Mirror rooms rarely come to auction, so their value is mostly seen in museums, not in the saleroom.

quotes.q: I write novels and poems, and I also paint in the hospital. They are my saviours.
quotes.who: Yayoi Kusama, quoted in Tate's Infinity Mirror Rooms exhibition guide

quotes.q: My wish was to be a painter one day.
quotes.who: Yayoi Kusama, Tate film, 2012

reading: Three questions sort Kusama prices: when was it made, what kind of object is it, and is it unique? A New York net of the early 1960s, a Pumpkin canvas of the 1990s and a signed screenprint are not comparable, even at the same house in the same week.

el-anatsui.summary: El Anatsui is a Ghanaian sculptor, born in Anyako in 1944, who has taught and worked in Nsukka, Nigeria, since 1975. He is best known for large wall hangings made from flattened aluminium bottle caps joined with copper wire. He received the Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement at the Venice Biennale in 2015.
body: Only two public auction lots from 2025 and 2026 could be documented, both at Sotheby's in London. G6 (2023) was offered on 4 March 2026 in a group of works donated by artists to support the Royal Academy, against an estimate of GBP 800,000 to 1.2 million. Artdaily reports GBP 742,400 (US$995,000), without naming the basis. Sotheby's shows the result only to signed-in users. Sotheby's rate since February 2026 is 28% on the first £1.5 million, and GBP 742,400 works back to a hammer price of exactly GBP 580,000, so we treat it as the price with premium and show the hammer as our calculation.

Hesitant Rivers (2012) closed on 16 October 2025 with the same estimate. Sotheby's shows the result only to signed-in users and we found no published report of it. We also tried Artnet and MutualArt, which refused automated visits, and auction summaries for that week. Whether it sold, and for how much, is still to confirm.

Two results are too few to describe his market. Artnet lists further lots offered in 2026, but shows their prices only to subscribers. The widely reported US$2.2 million sale of LuwVor I at Frieze New York in May 2026 was a gallery sale, not an auction, and is not in the table.
sources: Tate press release, Behind the Red Moon
Studio International, Veronica Simpson, El Anatsui interview (27 October 2023)
The Art Newspaper, Louisa Buck, El Anatsui on making art from waste (9 October 2023)
standing: El Anatsui received the Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement at the Venice Biennale in 2015 and the Praemium Imperiale in 2017. In October 2023 Tate Modern unveiled his Hyundai Commission, Behind the Red Moon, in the Turbine Hall, which Tate described as his largest work to date. Tate lists his work in the collections of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the British Museum, the Centre Pompidou and the Smithsonian's National Museum of African Art.
We could document only two auction lots from 2025 and 2026, so his museum record says far more about his standing than his auction record does.
career: Anatsui studied at the College of Art at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology in Kumasi from 1965 to 1968, then taught sculpture at the University of Nigeria in Nsukka for more than four decades, according to The Art Newspaper. Early work was carved wood and clay; a Danish residency produced driftwood sculptures such as Akua's Surviving Children (1996), according to Studio International.

The bottle-cap hangings brought international attention in the 2000s. October Gallery in London showed Man's Cloth and Woman's Cloth in 2002, and the British Museum acquired them. By 2007 such works were in the de Young Museum, the Centre Pompidou and the Metropolitan Museum of Art, and that year he showed Dusasa I and II at the Venice Biennale, according to Studio International.

works.m: Aluminium bottle caps and copper wire
works.note: Shown at October Gallery in London and bought by the British Museum. An early example of a museum acquiring the hangings soon after they were made.

works.m: Three-part installation, Tate Modern Turbine Hall
works.note: The Hyundai Commission, in three acts: The Red Moon, The World and The Wall. Works on this scale are made for institutions and do not come to auction.

works.m: Aluminium bottle caps and copper wire
works.note: A tall hanging with bands of colour running down it. Hangings of this kind are what reaches the saleroom, and size matters a great deal when comparing them.

quotes.q: When something has been used, there is a certain charge, a certain energy.
quotes.who: El Anatsui, The Art Newspaper, October 2023

quotes.q: Freedom is so very important, it can ameliorate so many things.
quotes.who: El Anatsui, on letting curators fold and hang his works, The Art Newspaper, October 2023

reading: Anatsui's hangings have no fixed shape. He lets each installer drape them differently, so a catalogue's dimensions describe one hanging, not the work for all time. Check whether a lot is a full wall hanging, a smaller relief or a wooden sculpture before comparing prices.

beatriz-milhazes.summary: Beatriz Milhazes is a Brazilian painter, born in Rio de Janeiro in 1960, where she still works. She paints motifs on plastic sheets and transfers them to canvas, building dense layers of flowers, circles and stripes.
body: The table lists the two unique works we could document from 2026. Phillips' lot page for Paraty gives "Sold For US$516,000" without naming the basis; we show it as the price with premium. Christie's lot page for Moinho vermelho (Red Mill), lot 5 in London on 25 June 2026, gives a price realised of GBP 584,200 against an estimate of GBP 600,000 to 800,000, so it sold below its low estimate.
Unsold lots are part of the record. Ovale (2002), a collage on paper offered by Phillips in New York with an estimate of US$30,000 to 50,000, shows no sold price on its lot page.

Editions are tracked separately. Bolha de Sabão (Soap Bubble), a 2024 collage edition of 40, sold for GBP 9,675 in a Phillips online editions sale in London in June 2026. It is not comparable with a unique canvas.
sources: Studio International, David Trigg, Beatriz Milhazes interview (12 July 2023)
Ocula, Beatriz Milhazes in conversation with Diana d'Arenberg (7 April 2015)
standing: Milhazes represented Brazil at the Venice Biennale in 2003. Her paintings are in the collections of the Museum of Modern Art, the Guggenheim and the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York. In São Paulo, MASP and Itaú Cultural held a joint survey of more than 170 works, Avenida Paulista, from December 2020 to mid 2021. In 2025 the Guggenheim gave her the first New York museum show devoted to her work, Rigor and Beauty.
On this site her highest documented results are for large unique canvases. Her collage editions sell at a very different level and are tracked separately.
career: Milhazes studied journalism before training at the Parque Lage School of Visual Arts in Rio, and took part in the 1984 exhibition Como Vai Você, Geração 80?, according to Studio International. She grew up under Brazil's military dictatorship of 1964 to 1985.

She developed her transfer technique in 1989 and began making collages in 2003, using sweet and chocolate wrappers, according to Ocula. Her first public commission was the facade of Selfridges in Manchester in 2004. In 2023 Turner Contemporary in Margate gave her Maresias, her first institutional show in the UK in more than 20 years.

works.note: One of her widest canvases, in the collection of the 'la Caixa' Foundation. Very large canvases from the early 2000s are the group that carries her highest prices.
199 x 195 cm, in the Cranford Collection. Our reading: a canvas so packed with circles, stripes and flowers that the eye never settles in one place.
Unique works on paper, separate from her print editions. They sell at a different level from the canvases and should be compared with each other.

quotes.q: I don't fear colour.
quotes.who: Beatriz Milhazes, Studio International, 2023

quotes.q: Yes, I'm shifting low art into high art.
quotes.who: Beatriz Milhazes, Ocula, 2015

reading: Three groups need keeping apart: canvases, unique collages and works on paper, and print editions. Within the canvases, compare size and date.

s-h-raza.summary: S.H. Raza (1922 to 2016) was an Indian painter who co-founded the Bombay Progressive Artists' Group in 1947 and lived in France from 1950 until about 2010. His early landscapes gave way, from 1980, to geometric paintings built around the bindu, a central black dot.
body: The table lists the five most recent public sales of unique works we could document, all from September 2026 and all checked against the auction houses' own lot pages. Prices are in Indian rupees. Saffronart states that its prices include the buyer's premium. AstaGuru labels its price for La Provence Noire "inclusive of margin" and does not use the term buyer's premium; we show it in the premium column on that basis.

Earlier 2026 results are not in the table, for example Origin (2000), sold by AstaGuru in August 2026 for INR 47,158,954 inclusive of margin. A Raza lithograph on StoryLTD showed only a current bid when we checked, so it is not included.
sources: The Art Newspaper, Raza at the Centre Pompidou
Christie's, 10 things to know about Sayed Haider Raza (3 September 2023)
Centre Pompidou, Sayed Haider Raza, les lieux de l'abstraction (15 December 2022)
standing: He received the Padma Shri in 1981, the Padma Bhushan in 2007 and the Padma Vibhushan in 2013, and France made him a Commandeur of the Légion d'honneur in 2015. In 2023 the Centre Pompidou in Paris held a retrospective of more than 90 works, which The Art Newspaper described as his first in a state-run institution.

His market is centred on Indian auction houses, which is why most of the prices here are in rupees. His French landscapes and his later bindu paintings are different bodies of work, so compare prices within one period.
career: Raza was born in 1922 in what is now Madhya Pradesh, the son of a forest ranger, moved to Bombay in 1943 and studied at the Sir J.J. School of Art, according to Christie's. In 1950 he took up a scholarship at the École des Beaux-Arts in Paris. He met the gallerist Lara Vincy in 1955 and won the Prix de la Critique in 1956, according to the Centre Pompidou.

He lived in France for about 60 years and taught at the University of California, Berkeley, in 1962, where he encountered Mark Rothko's painting. After the death of his wife, the French artist Janine Mongillat, he returned to India, according to Christie's. The bindu became systematic in his work from the 1980s.

works.note: One of his largest paintings. Christie's sold it in London on 10 June 2010 for £2,393,250, and The Art Newspaper reports it was bought by the Kiran Nadar Museum of Art.

Sold at Christie's New York on 21 March 2018 for US$4,452,500, which Christie's gives as his auction record. Christie's lists other results above US$1 million for paintings of the 1960s and 1970s, such as Village en Fête (1964) and La Terre (1973).
Geometric works built round a black dot. They exist in many sizes, so size is the first thing to compare.

quotes.q: The most tenacious memory of my childhood is the fear and fascination of Indian forests.
quotes.who: S.H. Raza, 2001, quoted by Christie's

quotes.q: It's the centre of my life.
quotes.who: S.H. Raza on the bindu, 2010, quoted by Christie's

reading: His prices are recorded in rupees, pounds and US dollars because he sells in Mumbai, Delhi, London and New York. We never convert them. Compare a rupee result with other rupee results, and keep the French landscapes, the dark 1960s and 1970s paintings and the bindu works apart.

gerhard-richter.summary: Gerhard Richter is a German painter, born in Dresden in 1932, who moved to West Germany in 1961 and lives in Cologne. He works in two main strands: blurred paintings made from photographs, and abstract paintings dragged across the canvas with a large squeegee.
body: The table lists the five most recent public sales of unique paintings we could document. Christie's Hong Kong sold Abstraktes Bild (1991) on 27 March 2026 for HKD 92,100,000 with premium, a hammer price of HKD 76,000,000, as reported by TheValue.

Two London results from October 2026 are added. Phillips sold Mathis (1983), from the collection of Marcel Brient, on 15 October for £5,839,000, just under its £6 million low estimate, according to its own lot page. The same evening Sotheby's sold Abstraktes Bild (1992), lot 19, for a hammer price of £5.4 million, according to The Art Newspaper. Sotheby's shows the total only to signed-in users. Its published rates turn that hammer into £6,678,000, which agrees with the £6.7 million reported with fees, so the table shows the total as our calculation.

Christie's gives US$35,135,000 with premium for Kerze (Candle) (1982). Working back from Christie's rates at the time gives a hammer price of exactly US$30,000,000, which matches The Art Newspaper's report of about US$30 million, so we show it as our calculation. The same paper reports Abstraktes Bild (1991), sold at Christie's New York on 19 November 2026, at a hammer price of US$7.6 million and US$9.4 million with fees. Christie's New York rates from September 2026 turn that hammer into US$9,392,000, shown as our calculation. A pre-sale listing of the evening sale gives its estimate as US$7 million to 10 million, so it sold inside the estimate; its lot page and lot number are still to confirm. Phillips' own lot page for Abstraktes Bild (522-1), lot 7 in Hong Kong on 30 September 2026, gives HKD 23,010,000 against HKD 18 million to 25 million. Christie's lot page for the 1992 Abstraktes Bild sold in London in March 2026, lot 672, gives GBP 355,600 against GBP 300,000 to 500,000.

Unsold lots are part of the record. At Christie's New York on 19 November 2026, bidding for Abstraktes Bild (1990) stopped at US$5.7 million against an estimate of US$6 million to 8 million, and it did not sell.
Photographs and overpainted photographs are tracked separately. Christie's sold Strip (2012) for US$1,765,300 with premium in May 2026.
sources: The Art Newspaper, Christie's New York, November 2026
Phillips press release, Hong Kong, September 2026
The Art Newspaper, Marian Goodman's Richters
Tate press release, Gerhard Richter: Panorama
The Art Newspaper, Sotheby's London, October 2026
The Met, Gerhard Richter: Painting After All
standing: Richter received the Praemium Imperiale for painting and the Golden Lion at the Venice Biennale, both in 1997. Tate Modern's retrospective, Gerhard Richter: Panorama, ran from 6 October 2011 to 8 January 2012, and Tate described him then as widely regarded as one of the most important artists working today. His stained glass window for Cologne Cathedral was unveiled in 2007.

In 2026 alone we list sales of his paintings in London, New York and Hong Kong. Prices depend on which strand of his work a piece belongs to, and on its size and date, so abstract paintings, photo paintings, photographs and editions should each be compared with their own kind. That is why photographs and overpainted photographs are kept out of the main table.
career: Richter left East Germany in 1961, aged 29, to study in Düsseldorf, according to the Metropolitan Museum of Art. The Met calls Table (1962) his first painting. He taught at the Düsseldorf academy from 1971 and moved to Cologne in 1983.

Museums have tracked both strands of his work for decades. The Met Breuer's Painting After All, from 4 March to 5 July 2020, showed over 100 works, from Table to Birkenau (2014), a cycle based on four photographs taken secretly at Auschwitz-Birkenau in 1944.

works.note: Painted from photographs and blurred with a dry brush. Kerze (Candle) of 1982 is one, and sold at Christie's New York in May 2026.
Paint pulled across the canvas with a large squeegee. Abstraktes Bild of 1991 sold at Christie's Hong Kong in March 2026 and is in the table above.
Started as figurative paintings from the 1944 photographs and painted over into abstraction. It shows how the two strands meet.

quotes.q: It's not unusual for me to start from the figurative and end up with something abstract.
quotes.who: Gerhard Richter, Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung, 2016, quoted by the Metropolitan Museum of Art

quotes.q: Helplessness is the great theme in painting, or rather the strongest motivation for and during painting.
quotes.who: Gerhard Richter, The Richter Interviews, quoted by the Metropolitan Museum of Art

reading: Check the strand, the date and the size before comparing two Richter results. A small abstract of the 2000s is not a guide to a large one of 1991, and neither says much about a photo painting.

osgemeos.summary: OSGEMEOS are the Brazilian twin brothers Gustavo and Otavio Pandolfo, born in 1974, who started as graffiti artists in São Paulo. Their murals, paintings and installations show thin, yellow-skinned figures in patterned clothes, often with sequins, sound or found doors.
body: The table lists the five most recent public sales of unique works we could document, each checked against the auction house's own lot page. Christie's shows a "Price realised", which under its usual terms includes the buyer's premium; Bonhams states "inc. premium". Phillips' lot pages give "Sold For" without naming the basis; we show it as the price with premium.

Unsold and unpriced lots are part of the record. I See The Light (2024) was sold by Phillips in London in October 2025 to benefit a charity, with no price published. All Connected (2020), offered at Sotheby's New York on 12 November 2024, shows its result only to signed-in users. An Untitled canvas of 2011, offered by Phillips in London on 30 June 2023 with an estimate of GBP 150,000 to 200,000, shows no sold price.
sources: Christie's lot 117, Sem medo de ser feliz
Phillips lot 390, O dia em que a Andorinha não voou
Phillips lot 495, Dentro do arco-iris, é assim
Phillips lot 225, I See The Light
Tate press release, Street Art at Tate Modern
NPR, 'We are like one artist' (19 September 2024)
Juxtapoz, OSGEMEOS reveal their secrets in major homecoming museum show (2020)
Jordan Schnitzer Museum of Art, Artist Resources: OSGEMEOS
standing: In 2008 OSGEMEOS were among six artists invited to paint the river front of Tate Modern for its Street Art exhibition, from 23 May to 25 August, which Tate called the first major public museum display of street art in London. Tate's release noted that they started painting graffiti in 1987.
Their murals stay on the walls they are painted on. What reaches auction is studio work: paintings, sculpture and installations, which is a much smaller pool.
career: The twins grew up in Cambuci, an old working-class neighbourhood of São Paulo, and invented an imaginary world as children that they call Tritrez, according to Juxtapoz and NPR. For the 2004 Athens Olympics they painted a giant figure about 82 feet high, NPR reports.

Museum shows have grown with them: Tate Modern and the Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo in 2008, a first US solo show at ICA Boston in 2012, Segredos at the Pinacoteca de São Paulo from 2020, which gathered more than 1,000 items, and Endless Story at the Hirshhorn in Washington from 29 September 2024, their first major museum survey in the United States.

works.m: Paint on a castle in Scotland
works.note: Murals like this stay where they are painted and are never sold. They build reputation, not a sales record.

works.m: Acrylic, spray enamel, latex and sequins on panel
works.note: A studio panel of the kind that does reach auction. It sold at Christie's in July 2026 and is in the table above.

quotes.q: We are like one artist.
quotes.who: Gustavo Pandolfo, NPR, 2024

reading: Their studio works mix paint with sequins, wood, sound and moving parts, so condition and completeness matter as much as size. Check that a work with sound or moving parts still works and is complete.

vhils.summary: Vhils is the Portuguese artist Alexandre Farto, born in Lisbon in 1987. He started in Lisbon graffiti and makes portraits by cutting, drilling, etching or blasting into walls, posters, doors and metal.
body: Only one unique work could be documented with a price: Attrition series #01, sold at Bonhams in London in October 2025 for GBP 10,240 including premium. Sotheby's sold carved works in 2025, among them Depict Series #08 and Logo and Pattern Series #03 in July, but shows their results only to signed-in users.

Editions are tracked separately. Four signed prints sold in Artcurial's Urban Online sale in Paris, which closed on 3 April 2026: Tenuous (screenprint, 73/250) EUR 1,986, Glimpse (lithograph, 81/140) EUR 1,258, Debris (screenprint, 165/300) EUR 861 and an untitled lithograph (13/25) EUR 596. Artcurial's pages show these as "Sold" without naming the basis.
sources: designboom, Vhils studio visit and interview (19 May 2017)
Euronews, Meet Vhils, Portugal's urban archaeologist (2022, updated 2024)
Hypebeast, Exploding Identity with Vhils (9 March 2020)
standing: Vhils has had institutional shows in his home city. MAAT in Lisbon showed Prisma, a video installation filmed in nine cities, from 30 March to 5 September 2022. In early 2026 MUDE, Lisbon's design museum, showed Selected Editions 2008-2024, a look back at his printed editions.
His carved walls stay where they are made, so his auction record is built from studio pieces and prints. Unique carved works and prints sell at very different levels.
career: Farto started as an illegal graffiti writer at 13 and by 16 or 17 was questioning it, he told designboom in 2017. He studied in London at about 19 and painted at the Cans Festival there in 2008, alongside Banksy, according to Euronews.
His studio, founded in 2010, works from Barreiro on the outskirts of Lisbon with a team of about 15, and he developed his explosives method around 2012, according to Hypebeast.

works.note: The wall works that made his name. They stay on the buildings and are never sold.
Studio pieces like Attrition series #01 are the unique works that reach auction. This one is in the table above.
The editions we have seen at Artcurial were numbered in runs of 25 to 300. They sell often and at much lower levels, so they are tracked apart from unique works.

quotes.q: All of the layers in my work were a part of someone's life before.
quotes.who: Vhils, Hypebeast, March 2020

reading: Read the medium line first. Carved posters, carved wood or metal, explosive works and prints are all sold under his name, and they are priced very differently.

kaws.summary: KAWS is the American artist Brian Donnelly, born in 1974. He began by tagging walls in New Jersey and Manhattan and painting cartoon figures onto bus shelter adverts, and is known for COMPANION, a figure with crossed-out eyes, in paintings, sculpture, prints and toys.
body: The table lists the five most recent public sales of unique paintings, plus one sculpture from an edition of three, found at Phillips and Christie's. KAWS sells at many houses every week; Sotheby's and smaller houses were not checked. Christie's shows a "Price realised", which under its usual terms includes the buyer's premium. Phillips' "Sold For" figure is shown as the price with premium.

COMPANION (ORIGINALFAKE), 3 of 3, sold at Christie's London in June 2026 for GBP 228,600, below its low estimate of GBP 350,000. KILL SITE (2019), offered at Christie's New York, shows no published result on its lot page.

Editions are tracked separately. At Phillips in October 2026, the three-screenprint set NO REPLY sold for USD 12,900 and a printer's proof of YOU SHOULD KNOW I KNOW for USD 7,740. The same SHARE screenprint (edition 500) made GBP 3,072 at Christie's London online in September 2026 and USD 17,780 at a Christie's online sale in July 2026.
sources: Christie's lot 233, CAMO CAN'T HELP YOU
Phillips lot 298, YOU SHOULD KNOW I KNOW
The Brooklyn Rail, KAWS with Jason Rosenfeld (June 2021)
The Art Newspaper, The Big Review: Kaws at the Brooklyn Museum (9 April 2021)
standing: The Brooklyn Museum gave KAWS a survey, KAWS: WHAT PARTY, from 26 February to 5 September 2021, with more than 100 works from early graffiti drawings and altered adverts to large COMPANION sculptures.

His market is unusually wide. He sells paintings, sculpture, prints and toys, and his name appears at many auction houses every week. That makes it especially important to separate unique paintings from editions and collectibles when reading his prices.
career: Before the toys, KAWS painted his own figures over adverts in bus shelters. Untitled (Haring) of 1997 is one, painted on an existing advertising poster and first shown at a friend's restaurant gallery in Seattle, according to the Brooklyn Rail. In 2006 he made ORIGINALFAKE COMPANION for his shop in Tokyo.
His first sculpture-only show was at CAC Málaga in 2014, and in 2021 KAWS: WHAT PARTY at the Brooklyn Museum was his first museum show in New York, according to the Brooklyn Rail.

works.note: The same figure exists as a mass-produced toy, as sculptures in editions of a few and as giant inflatables. Only the sculptures and paintings belong in a table of unique or near-unique works.

works.m: Acrylic on canvas in a blister package
works.note: Small paintings sealed in toy-style packaging. He said he made about 40 of the smaller ones in 2002.

quotes.q: I think no matter what I put on canvas, people don't think of me as a painter.
quotes.who: KAWS, the Brooklyn Rail, June 2021

reading: With KAWS the first job is sorting. Collectible toys, open editions (The Art Newspaper reported some priced at US$250), numbered prints, sculpture editions and unique paintings are all different markets. The table lists unique paintings and one sculpture from an edition of three.

eko-nugroho.summary: Eko Nugroho is an Indonesian artist, born in 1977, who lives and works in Yogyakarta. He makes murals, paintings, embroidery, batik and sculpture, with masked comic-book figures, often working with local communities.
body: Only three sales of unique works could be documented, all checked on the auction houses' own pages. Christie's shows a "Price realised", which under its usual terms includes the buyer's premium; Phillips' "Sold For" figure is shown as the price with premium. Topi untuk Haring sold well below its low estimate.

Unsold and unpriced lots are part of the record. Garden Full of Blooming Democracy #9 (2017), offered by Phillips in Hong Kong on 29 March 2025 with an estimate of HKD 120,000 to 180,000, shows no sold price. Seneng Kuwi Larang Regane (2009), offered at Sotheby's Hong Kong in November 2021, shows its result only to signed-in users. Indonesian auction houses were not checked.
sources: Christie's lot 76, Trap Costum for President 1
Christie's lot 75, Empty Kitchen for 5 Months #04
Phillips lot 60, Garden Full of Blooming Democracy #9
The Jakarta Post, Eko Nugroho: Recording History through Art (14 January 2017)
Art + Australia, Rifky Effendy, Reality in the World of Eko Nugroho
standing: Eko Nugroho was one of five artists chosen for Indonesia's pavilion at the 55th Venice Biennale in 2013, where he showed a bamboo raft work, Menghasut Badai-badai (Instigating Storms).
His auction record outside Indonesia is thin. We have not yet checked Indonesian auction houses, so the picture here is incomplete.
career: Nugroho studied at the Indonesian Institute of the Arts in Yogyakarta and founded the comic magazine Daging Tumbuh in 2000. His first solo show was at Cemeti Art House in 2002, according to The Jakarta Post.

From 2006 his work reached international museums: the Asia Pacific Triennial in Brisbane, a solo show at the Musée d'Art Moderne de Paris in 2012 and the Indonesian Pavilion at the Venice Biennale in 2013. In 2013 he also designed a Louis Vuitton scarf, made in an edition of 500, The Jakarta Post reports.

works.note: Stitched by tailors from his designs; he has said finding people who could do it was hard at first. Illusion (2007) is in the Singapore Art Museum, and Trap Costum for President 1 (2011) is in our table.
Creamy policy (2010) is a typical example, 200 x 150 cm. Paintings and embroideries sell at different levels and should be compared within their own group.

quotes.q: I don't want to pass judgment on somebody. Such cases can happen to anybody in the future.
quotes.who: Eko Nugroho on why his figures wear masks, The Jakarta Post, 2017

reading: Our record has three results, at Christie's in London and Phillips in Hong Kong, in two currencies. That is too few to describe a level, so treat each price as a single result.

faith-xlvii.summary: Faith XLVII is a South African artist, born in 1979, who began writing graffiti as Faith47 in 1997 and has painted public murals in 39 countries. She also makes prints, hand-sewn hangings, bronzes and paintings.
body: The table lists the two works on panel or found paper we could document, both sold by Strauss & Co in South Africa. Strauss states that its prices include buyer's premium and VAT, so they are shown in the premium column on that basis. The triptych did not sell when first offered on 15 April 2024 and sold two months later for ZAR 29,313 with fees, under its ZAR 30,000 low estimate.

Editions are tracked separately. Strauss sold Ex Animo (2017, screenprint, 21/47) for ZAR 9,369 on 13 July 2026, and two lithograph proofs, Omnia in Mensura et Numero et Pondere Disposuisti (ZAR 5,863) and CAPAX INFINITI (ZAR 5,277), on 25 October 2022.
sources: Strauss & Co lot 332, Coltan; Oil; Diamonds
Strauss & Co lot 511, Ons vir Jou Suid-Afrika
Strauss & Co lot 153, Omnia in Mensura
Daily Maverick, CHANT: Faith XLVII's public practice (22 April 2020)
standing: In 2025 the STRAAT Museum in Amsterdam showed ORIGINS: Family & Legacy, from 18 April to 8 June, with work by Faith XLVII, her son and another artist, and added one of her works to its collection. Artdaily reports that her work has also been shown at the Brooklyn Museum.
Her murals stay where they are painted and do not come to auction. Her auction record so far is in South Africa and is small.
career: Faith XLVII was born in Cape Town and sprayed her first wall at the old Clovelly train station, according to Daily Maverick. She was among the most prolific names on the South African scene in the late 1990s and early 2000s, and by 2020 had been based in Los Angeles for three years.
Her murals now cover walls in 39 countries, according to Strauss & Co. In 2025 the STRAAT Museum in Amsterdam gave her a show and added a work to its collection.

works.m: Mural, Portland, Oregon; later a lithograph
works.note: The wall cannot be sold, but the lithograph of the same image can. That is how many street artists' public images reach the market.
A studio work in hand-made frames, named after resources mined in Africa. Sold at Strauss & Co in June 2024 and in the table above.

quotes.q: These are not works made to be pretty or decorative; these are works made to consider, to dismantle, to question.
quotes.who: Faith XLVII on her exhibition CHANT, Daily Maverick, April 2020

reading: Her public results are few and mostly in rand, at Strauss & Co in South Africa. A short record in one currency cannot show a trend.

vincent-van-gogh.summary: Vincent van Gogh was a Dutch painter, born in Zundert in 1853, who died at Auvers-sur-Oise in France on 29 July 1890. In just over ten years he made about 2,100 works, around 860 of them oil paintings, most in the last two years of his life. He is known for bold colour and fast, visible brushwork.
body: We have documented one sale so far, the auction record set in New York this November. Sotheby's sold Châtaigniers en fleurs (Chestnut Trees in Blossom), painted in Auvers on 24 May 1890, as lot 5 of the Blaquier-Arrieta collection on 18 November 2026. The estimate was given only on request. Art Insider reports US$190.4 million with fees and a hammer price of US$165 million. The Art Newspaper gives the same hammer price. Sotheby's shows the result only to signed-in users. Its published New York rates turn a US$165 million hammer into US$190,430,000, which agrees with the reported US$190.4 million, so the table shows that total as our calculation.

The previous record for the artist was US$117.2 million for Orchard with Cypresses (1888), sold at Christie's New York in 2022. The sale went ahead under an agreement between the seller and the heirs of Samuel and Hedwig Fischer, who owned the painting from 1909 until it was sold in 1936. Our report on the November 2026 New York sales, under Research Reports, sets it beside the other top lots of the week.

The Kröller-Müller Museum in Otterlo holds a smaller painting of the same subject, Blossoming Chestnut Trees, dated 22 to 23 May 1890. The museum describes flat strokes of green, short dark blue strokes giving the leaves structure and a sky of overlapping zigzag marks. Earlier auction results for Van Gogh will be added here once we have checked them.
sources: Art Insider, Van Gogh record at Sotheby's
Buenos Aires Herald, the Blaquier Van Gogh
WebExhibits, Van Gogh's letters, letter 649 (about 10 July 1890)
WebExhibits, Van Gogh's letters, letter 651 (23 July 1890)
standing: Van Gogh had little success while he lived. His standing rests on more than a century of museum shows and scholarship since his death. Sotheby's lot page alone lists exhibitions of Châtaigniers en fleurs from Vollard's gallery in Paris in 1896 to the Fondation Louis Vuitton in 2026.

Very few major paintings by him come up for sale, and he made only about 70 oils in his weeks at Auvers. That scarcity is part of why one painting from May 1890 could make a price this high. It is not a guide to what his drawings or earlier paintings make.
career: Van Gogh painted for just over ten years. He left the asylum at Saint-Rémy on 16 May 1890 and made about 70 oil paintings in Auvers-sur-Oise before his death there on 29 July.

His letters to his brother Theo are the main record of how he worked. In July 1890 he described new canvases of open fields and wrote that they would show Theo how healthy and invigorating he found the countryside.

works.t: Châtaigniers en fleurs (Chestnut Trees in Blossom)
works.note: Painted at Auvers in May 1890 and sold at Sotheby's New York on 18 November 2026, setting his auction record. A painting from the final months with a long exhibition history is the rarest kind of Van Gogh to come up.
He called his sketch of it one of his most carefully thought-out canvases in a letter of 23 July 1890. Versions are in museum collections.

quotes.q: They are vast stretches of corn under troubled skies, and I did not have to go out of my way very much in order to try to express sadness and extreme loneliness.
quotes.who: Vincent van Gogh to Theo and Jo van Gogh, Auvers, about 10 July 1890 (letter 649, WebExhibits edition)

reading: Drawings, early Dutch paintings and late French paintings are separate markets. Very few late oils remain in private hands, so a price for one says little about a drawing or a painting from his Nuenen years.

wassily-kandinsky.summary: Wassily Kandinsky was born in Moscow in 1866 and died at Neuilly-sur-Seine, near Paris, in 1944. He trained in law and economics before turning to painting at 30, moved to Munich in 1896 and from about 1908 began to strip recognisable things out of his paintings until only colour, line and shape were left. He taught at the Bauhaus in Germany until it closed in 1933.
body: Two of the highest prices of autumn 2026 were for Kandinsky. At Christie's London on 14 October, Das bunte Leben (1907), a painting from his Munich years, sold for a hammer price of £27 million, £31,560,000 with fees, according to The Art Newspaper and London Art Walk. The Art Newspaper gives the high estimate as £25 million and My Modern Met gives £18 million to 25 million. Our table previously showed a high estimate of £35 million, which no source supports, and is now corrected. The lot number is still to confirm.

At Christie's New York on 17 November, Betonte Ecken (1922 to 1923) set his auction record. Christie's lot page, lot 12 A, gives a price realised of US$85,780,000 against US$60 million to 80 million, and The Art Newspaper gives the hammer price as US$74 million. Christie's New York rates from September 2026 turn that hammer into exactly the published total. The previous record, US$44.8 million for Murnau mit Kirche II (1910), was set at Sotheby's London in 2023.

Betonte Ecken has a museum past. Hilla Rebay acquired it in 1929 and gave it to the Guggenheim in 1941. The museum sold it at auction in London in 1964 for £22,000, and it sold again at Sotheby's New York in 1986 for US$1 million, according to Artsy and Art Insider. Our report on the November 2026 New York sales, under Research Reports, covers the rest of the week.
sources: The Art Newspaper, Christie's New York, November 2026
London Art Walk, Frieze week results
Tate, Paintings by Kandinsky from the Solomon R Guggenheim Museum
The Art Newspaper, Christie's London, October 2026
My Modern Met, Das bunte Leben
Project Gutenberg, Wassily Kandinsky, Concerning the Spiritual in Art
standing: Solomon R. Guggenheim began collecting Kandinsky in 1929 and met him at the Bauhaus in Dessau the next year, and Tate showed paintings from the Guggenheim's collection of his work in London in 1958. In 1911 he founded the Blue Rider group with Franz Marc, and his 1912 book On the Spiritual in Art set out how colour could carry an artist's inner concerns to the viewer.

Tate divides his work into a freer, expressive phase from 1909 to 1918 and a tighter, geometric one from 1921 to 1935. Betonte Ecken comes from the second. Both 2026 results carry well-documented histories, which helps explain their prices.
career: Kandinsky thought of painting in musical terms. Between 1909 and 1914 he wrote four stage works he called colour-tone dramas, among them The Yellow Sound, none staged in his lifetime, and in 1913 he published Klänge (Sounds), a book of 56 woodcuts and prose poems, according to the Guggenheim Bilbao.

At the Bauhaus he published Point and Line to Plane in 1926, and in 1928 designed a stage version of Mussorgsky's Pictures at an Exhibition at the Friedrich Theater in Dessau, which the Guggenheim in New York recreated in 2012.

works.note: From the start of his Bauhaus years. Once owned by the Guggenheim, it set his auction record at Christie's New York in November 2026. Museum provenance like this is part of what buyers pay for.
Coloured circles on a dark ground, in the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum. Many of his key paintings are in museums and will not come up for sale.

quotes.q: Every work of art is the child of its age and, in many cases, the mother of our emotions.
quotes.who: Wassily Kandinsky, Concerning the Spiritual in Art (Michael Sadler's English translation, Project Gutenberg)

reading: Oil paintings, watercolours, drawings and prints by Kandinsky are separate markets. Within the oils, the expressive years before 1914 and the geometric Bauhaus years are often compared, but each period is best compared with its own.

rene-matic.summary: Rene Matić was born in Peterborough in 1997, graduated from Central Saint Martins in 2020 and is based in London. The work is mostly photographs of family, friends and community, shown alongside sound, flags and banners.
body: We have not found a priced auction result for a unique work by Rene Matić. The one public sale we could document is a photograph, Pink Shoes at a Party (2023, archival pigment print, 150 x 101.6 cm), offered as lot 3 in the Whitechapel Gallery Art Icon charity online auction at Phillips, London, from 12 to 19 March 2024. The lot page marks it as sold but prints no price and no edition size, so it is not in the table.
That leaves nothing to compare. A first priced result, when one appears, will be a single data point, not a market.
sources: Phillips lot page, Pink Shoes at a Party
1854 Photography, Rene Matić wins the 2026 Deutsche Börse Photography Foundation Prize
Museums Association, Nnena Kalu celebrates Turner Prize win (December 2025)
University of the Arts London, Central Saint Martins graduate shortlisted for the Turner Prize 2025
Deutsche Börse, Rene Matić wins the Deutsche Börse Photography Foundation Prize 2026 (15 May 2026)
standing: Shortlisted for the Turner Prize 2025 for the solo exhibition AS OPPOSED TO THE TRUTH at CCA Berlin. The prize went to Nnena Kalu on 9 December 2025. The same exhibition won Matić the £30,000 Deutsche Börse Photography Foundation Prize in 2026. University of the Arts London describes Matić as the second-youngest artist nominated for the Turner Prize.
career: Matić is an artist and writer whose practice spans photography, film and sculpture, according to the Deutsche Börse Photography Foundation. Solo shows include fags for countries that don't exist but bodies that do at Arcadia Missa in 2021, soul time at Studio Voltaire in 2022, upon this rock at the South London Gallery in 2022, a girl for the living room at the Martin Parr Foundation in 2023 and JAZZ, with Oscar Murillo, at Kunsthalle Wien in 2024.

works.m: Photographs, installation and sound, CCA Berlin
works.note: The exhibition that was shortlisted for the Turner Prize 2025 and won the £30,000 Deutsche Börse Photography Foundation Prize in 2026. Prizes are given to exhibitions, not to works for sale.

reading: The Deutsche Börse release lists Matić's work in the collections of Tate, Fondation Louis Vuitton, the UK Government Art Collection and the Arts Council Collection. Museum and prize recognition of this kind is documented here, but it is not a price and should not be read as one.

raven-halfmoon.summary: Raven Halfmoon was born in Norman, Oklahoma, in 1991 and still works there. She is a citizen of the Caddo Nation and builds large figures in stoneware by coiling clay, some of them over 12 feet tall.
body: Two public auction results are documented, both at Phillips in New York in 2024 and both for stoneware sculptures made in 2020. On 15 May 2024, OKLA HOMMA OHOYO (lot 310) sold for US$22,860 with buyer's premium against an estimate of US$10,000 to 15,000. On 25 September 2024, Two Sides To Every Story and Historic Glory (lot 55) sold for US$20,320 with buyer's premium against the same estimate. Phillips does not print hammer prices on its lot pages, so those stay to confirm.
Two results are too few to describe a trend. Her largest works are documented in museums rather than at auction: Crystal Bridges bought Caddo Woman Warrior (2021) in 2024.
sources: Phillips lot page, OKLA HOMMA OHOYO
Phillips lot page, Two Sides To Every Story and Historic Glory
The Contemporary Austin, Raven Halfmoon: Flags of Our Mothers
The Art Newspaper, Raven Halfmoon brings her giant doubles to Ballroom Marfa (6 July 2026)
Southwest Contemporary, 8,000 Pounds of Clay with My Hands (1 September 2023)
The Creative Independent, Raven Halfmoon on being true to who you are (24 October 2024)
standing: Her first travelling solo exhibition, Flags of Our Mothers, opened at the Aldrich Contemporary Art Museum in 2023 and went on to the Bemis Center (2024), The Contemporary Austin (2025), the Ogden Museum of Southern Art (2025 to 2026) and Ballroom Marfa (2026). She was a 2023 Eiteljorg Contemporary Art Fellow and a 2024 LOEWE Craft Prize finalist, and was in the 2026 Whitney Biennial. Crystal Bridges, the Detroit Institute of Arts and ICA Miami hold her work.
career: Halfmoon holds a bachelor's degree in anthropology and studio art from the University of Arkansas, and is a citizen of the Caddo Nation who also has Choctaw, Delaware and Otoe heritage, according to The Creative Independent. In 2024 she added bronze and stone to her stoneware, and showed NEESH + SOKU (MOON + SUN) at Salon 94, her first show with the gallery.

works.note: Her largest figures are made for museum shows such as Flags of Our Mothers. Firing alone takes two to three weeks, she told Southwest Contemporary.
One of her first bronzes. Bronze can be cast in editions, so check the edition when one appears at auction.

quotes.q: I went through about 8,000 pounds of clay with my hands.
quotes.who: Raven Halfmoon, on making Flags of Our Mothers, Southwest Contemporary, 2023

reading: Her two documented results are both for stoneware figures of 2020 at Phillips. Stoneware, bronze and travertine are different materials with different costs and editions, so they should not be compared with one another.

ana-segovia.summary: Ana Segovia was born in Mexico City in 1991 and works there. Segovia paints in oil, mostly figures taken from Mexican cowboy imagery and golden-age cinema, and has recently added video and charcoal drawing.
body: We have found no public auction result for Ana Segovia as of 25 November 2026. That does not mean no work has ever been sold at auction, only that none is documented in the sources we checked.

The record so far is a gallery one. kurimanzutto announced on 15 November 2023 that Segovia had joined the gallery, and gave the artist a solo booth at Frieze London in October 2025. We found no published gallery prices. Gallery prices and auction prices are different things and are not compared here.
sources: kurimanzutto, Ana Segovia joins kurimanzutto (15 November 2023)
Galerie, Next Big Thing: Ana Segovia (28 November 2025)
AnOther, Ana Segovia's Erotic Cowboy Paintings Reframe the Male Body (24 October 2025)
La Biennale di Venezia, Ana Segovia (2024)
standing: MOCA Los Angeles gave Segovia a solo exhibition, MOCA Focus, from 23 November 2024 to 4 May 2025, and bought Through Mario's perspective (2024). Segovia showed in the 60th Venice Biennale in 2024. kurimanzutto lists works in the Louisiana Museum of Modern Art, the Denver Art Museum and the Pérez Art Museum Miami.
career: Segovia's paintings start from film stills of the golden age of Mexican cinema, from the mid-1930s to the late 1950s, and from classic Westerns, according to Galerie. In 2024 the Venice Biennale showed Pos' se acabó este cantar (2021), Segovia's first film, with two charros in suits made by the grandson of Jorge Negrete's tailor.
In 2025 kurimanzutto gave Segovia a solo booth at Frieze London with the Ramón series, built around an invented Mexican cowboy, according to AnOther.

works.note: An early painting, cited by Galerie as part of the film-based work.
Paintings of one invented cowboy, shown at Frieze London. Fair sales are gallery sales; their prices are rarely published and are not auction results.

quotes.q: I'm always thinking about three things in art that are important to my process: humor, eros, and aggression.
quotes.who: Ana Segovia, AnOther, October 2025

dana-awartani.summary: Dana Awartani was born in Jeddah in 1987 and lives between Jeddah and New York. Trained in traditional Islamic arts, she works with geometry, embroidery, natural dyes and tile, often to address the loss of heritage.
body: No auction result for a unique work by Dana Awartani has been confirmed on an auction house page, so the table is empty. Three lots were found.

At Sotheby's, Dodecahedron Within an Icosahedron (2016, wood, copper and glass, number 3 from an edition of 3 plus an artist's proof) was offered as lot 1 in October 2019 against an estimate of £18,000 to 22,000. Sotheby's shows the result only to signed-in readers, so it is to confirm. As an edition, it would not go in our table of unique works.

At Christie's New York, Abjad Hawaz Series (2016, shell gold, ink and gouache on paper, in 28 parts) was offered on 14 December 2022 (lot 244) and again on 18 December 2024 (lot 228). The listings database Very Important Lot reports the 2024 offer as sold for US$6,930 and gives no result for 2022. We have not been able to check either on Christie's own pages, so both stay to confirm.

career: Awartani trained at Central Saint Martins and the Prince's School of Traditional Arts in London, according to Berlin Art Link. She works with craftspeople, including natural dyers in Trivandrum in South India and Syrian refugees in Jordan, and has said she makes no duplicates.

works.t: Come, let me heal your wounds. Let me mend your broken bones
works.m: Silk dyed with herbs and spices, torn and darned
works.note: Shown at the 60th Venice Biennale. Installations of this size are made for exhibitions and rarely reach auction.

works.m: Shell gold, ink and gouache on paper, in 28 parts
works.note: Offered at Christie's New York in 2022 and again in 2024. Works on paper like this are the kind that do reach the saleroom.

quotes.q: Nothing is mass-produced and I don't make duplicates.
quotes.who: Dana Awartani, Berlin Art Link, November 2025

jes-fan.summary: Jes Fan was born in Toronto in 1990, grew up in Hong Kong, trained in glass at the Rhode Island School of Design, and works between Brooklyn and Hong Kong. The sculptures combine glass, resin and 3D-printed body parts with materials such as melanin and testosterone.
body: We have found no public auction result for Jes Fan as of 25 November 2026. That does not mean no work has been sold at auction, only that none is documented in the sources we checked.

andy-warhol.summary: Andy Warhol was an American artist, born Andrew Warhola in Pittsburgh on 6 August 1928, who died in New York on 22 February 1987. He worked as a commercial illustrator in New York in the 1950s, then made his name in the early 1960s with paintings of soup cans, film stars and news photographs, most of them printed onto canvas by photo-silkscreen.
body: The table lists the five most recent sales of unique works we could document, newest first. Four of them were sold in one night, 16 November 2026, at Sotheby's New York, and one three days later at Christie's.

Christie's lists Campbell's Soup Can (Turkey Noodle) (1962), from the collection of Antonio Homem Sonnabend, as sold on 19 November 2026 for US$9,026,000 against an estimate of US$6 million to 8 million. The Art Newspaper gives a hammer price of US$7.3 million. Christie's New York rates from September 2026 turn that hammer into exactly US$9,026,000, so the two sources agree. We have seen Christie's results listing for this lot but not the full lot page, so its lot number and medium are still to confirm.

Sotheby's shows its results only to signed-in users, so the four Sotheby's prices rest on press reports, while the lot numbers, sizes, media and estimates come from Sotheby's own lot pages. The 48 inch Flowers (lot 112), one of seven paintings of that size according to Sotheby's, made a hammer price of US$15.2 million and US$18.2 million with fees, according to The Art Newspaper. Sotheby's 2026 New York rates turn that hammer into US$18,160,000, shown as our calculation. Artdaily reports the 24 inch Flowers of 1964 (lot 101, from the collection of Beverly Grossman) at US$6.1 million and Dolly Parton (lot 124) at US$4.1 million, both well above their high estimates, but gives no hammer prices, so both totals stay to confirm.

The Scream (After Munch) (1984), lot 7 of the Baum collection sale earlier the same evening, is reported at US$7.9 million with fees by The Art Newspaper and by Luxury.it. The Art Newspaper also gives a hammer price of US$6.8 million, but Sotheby's published rates would turn that into about US$8.4 million, not US$7.9 million. Because the figures do not agree, we leave both the hammer and the total to confirm. Sotheby's lot page marks the work as guaranteed with irrevocable bids.

Two lots did not sell. Sotheby's lot page for Double Liz (lot 126) shows it as withdrawn from the 16 November sale, and The Art Newspaper reports that Christie's withdrew a Warhol self portrait, estimated at US$14 million to 18 million, from its 20th Century Evening Sale on 17 November.

Works on paper and prints are tracked separately, following our guide on unique works and editions. On 19 November Christie's sold The Kiss (Bela Lugosi) (1963), silkscreen ink on paper, for US$4,634,000 against US$3 million to 5 million. Phillips' own lot page shows Ten Portraits of Jews of the Twentieth Century (1980), a set of ten screenprints numbered 103 from an edition of 200, sold for US$1,096,500 on 17 November, against US$400,000 to 600,000. MyArtBroker reports its hammer at US$850,000 and a complete set of Endangered Species (1983) hammered at its US$2.5 million low estimate at Sotheby's on 16 November.
standing: The Museum of Modern Art in New York owns Campbell's Soup Cans (1962), the 32 canvases first shown at the Ferus Gallery in Los Angeles in July 1962, and Tate in London owns Marilyn Diptych (1962). The Andy Warhol Museum in Pittsburgh is described as the largest museum in the United States devoted to a single artist.

His market is one of the deepest of any post-war artist. Christie's own search lists 5,892 sold lots by him, from paintings and drawings to prints and photographs. So a Warhol price only means something when it is compared with the same kind of work: a unique canvas, a print from an edition of 250 and a Polaroid sit in different markets.

features.title: New York, November 2026: The Top Lots and Why They Sold
features.standfirst: A US$190.4 million Van Gogh, a Kandinsky record and a week of guaranteed lots. The main sales, the twelve top prices and what lay behind them.
features.description: The November 2026 New York evening sales at Christie's, Sotheby's and Phillips: sale totals, the twelve highest prices with hammer and fees kept apart, why the top lots sold as they did, and the autumn sales in London and Hong Kong.
features.body:
Between 16 and 19 November 2026 the three largest auction houses held their autumn evening sales in New York. A Van Gogh made US$190.4 million, a new record for the artist, and records also fell for Kandinsky, Kusama and Sam Francis. Below are the main sales, the top lots and, as far as the sources allow, why they made what they did.

How to read the figures

Most prices in this piece were reported by the press, not read on the auction house's own lot page. Sotheby's shows results only to signed-in users, and Christie's lot pages refused our automated visits this week. Where only a reported, rounded figure exists we say so. Two exceptions in the top lots: Phillips' lot page gives the exact price for the Modigliani, and Christie's lot page for Kandinsky's Betonte Ecken, read after this report first appeared, gives US$85,780,000.

Every figure is in US dollars, because every sale here was in New York. "With fees" means the hammer price plus the buyer's premium, the fee the buyer pays the house. In New York this autumn Christie's and Sotheby's both charged 28% of the hammer up to US$2 million, 22% from there to US$8 million and 15% above. Our guide to the buyer's premium explains the bands.

Sotheby's titled its own video of the Blaquier-Arrieta sale "$412M Night". Estimates exclude fees, so compare them with the hammer total, not the total with fees.

The top lots

These are the twelve highest prices with fees that we could find for the week. As with every sales table on this site, the rows run newest first. The first column gives each lot's place by price.

Swipe sideways to see every column.

By priceWorkSaleEstimateHammerWith fees

The Giacometti and the Monet are given as about US$26m because the reports disagree by a few tens of thousands of dollars. Pissarro's La Place du Théâtre-Français, at a reported US$24.2m, sits just outside the twelve. Picasso's Le Baiser is reported as US$31.1m by The Art Newspaper and US$31.2m by Artdaily.

Why the top lots made what they did

No report can say for certain why a bidder paid a price. What the sources do show is a set of features that the highest prices share, and that the lower ones often lacked.

The moment in the artist's life

Van Gogh painted Châtaigniers en fleurs in Auvers on 24 May 1890, according to Sotheby's lot page, about nine weeks before he died. He made about 70 oil paintings in roughly as many days in Auvers, so the supply of work from those weeks is small. The painting also has a long public history: the lot page lists exhibitions from Vollard's gallery in Paris in 1896 to the Fondation Louis Vuitton this year. It beat the previous Van Gogh record, US$117.2 million for Orchard with Cypresses at Christie's in 2022, by more than US$70 million.

Kandinsky's Betonte Ecken comes from his first years teaching at the Bauhaus, when his painting turned to hard-edged geometric forms. Kusama's No. 3P.B., which set her record at US$15 million with fees on 16 November, is one of her earliest Infinity Nets and was shown at the Whitney Museum in 1961.

Provenance and long ownership

Many of the top works had been off the market for decades, and their history of ownership was published in detail. Betonte Ecken was bought by Hilla Rebay in 1929 and given to the Guggenheim in 1941. The museum sold it in London in 1964 for £22,000, and it sold again at Sotheby's New York in 1986 for US$1 million, according to Artsy and Art Insider. At the Baum sale, Joan Mitchell's Green Book of Barbara Guest made US$19.3 million with fees. The Baums had bought it in 1986 for US$65,000.

At Phillips, Robert Manley told The Art Newspaper that nearly 90% of the works offered had never been sold at auction before. A work that is new to the market has no earlier price to anchor the bidding.

Clear title

The Van Gogh nearly did not sell cleanly. Heirs of the Berlin publisher Samuel Fischer, who owned it from 1909, said the family had been forced to sell it in 1936 under Nazi persecution. Sotheby's announced a settlement the day before the sale, and the lot was sold under an agreement between the seller and the Fischer heirs. A painting with an open claim against it is very hard to sell at any price. Our guide to provenance explains why.

Guarantees

A guarantee means that someone, the house or a third party, has promised to buy the work at an agreed price if no one bids more. At Christie's 20th Century sale 31 lots carried third-party guarantees and five were guaranteed by the house, out of 75. At Phillips 14 of 22 lots were guaranteed. Sotheby's lot page marks the Van Gogh as guaranteed property with irrevocable bids, and Artsy reports a third-party guarantee on the Kandinsky. A guaranteed lot is close to certain to sell, which helps explain high sell-through rates. It says less about how many people wanted the work. Our guide to guarantees and catalogue symbols has more.

Competition on the night

The Kandinsky opened at US$54 million and three bidders competed, according to Artsy. The Klimt went to a telephone bidder after nearly six minutes, said Christie's. The Modigliani rose from US$18 million to US$28 million within seconds and went on to a ten-minute contest between three bidders, The Art Newspaper reported. Two or more determined bidders are what take a price past its estimate.

Where prices fell short

The week was not uniformly strong, and the misses are part of the record.

  • Picasso's Le Baiser, consigned by Jeff Koons according to The Art Newspaper, made US$31.1 million with fees against an estimate of US$40 million to 60 million. Koons had bought it in 2008 for US$17.4 million.
  • Six of the twelve Blaquier-Arrieta lots sold below their low estimates, Art Insider reported. Pissarro's view of the Place du Théâtre-Français made a reported US$24.2 million against US$30 million to 40 million.
  • De Kooning's Water...Soft Banks and a Window (Untitled VIII) hammered at US$17.1 million, below its US$20 million low estimate.
  • Franz Kline's Figure (1955) hammered at US$1.8 million against US$4 million to 6 million at the Baum sale.
  • At Christie's 21st Century sale, bidding for Gerhard Richter's Abstraktes Bild (1990) stopped at US$5.7 million against US$6 million to 8 million, and it did not sell.

The New York adviser Ralph DeLuca put it simply to The Art Newspaper: estimates that week were "a little aspirational". A price below estimate does not mean a work is poor. It may mean the estimate was set high to win the consignment.

Records

Artsy counted 20 new artist auction records in the week. Beyond Van Gogh, Kandinsky and Kusama, they include Sam Francis (Towards Disappearance I, US$17.1 million), Aaron Douglas (Harriet Tubman, US$14.48 million against US$2.5 million to 3.5 million), Cornelis Cornelisz van Haarlem (Hercules and Achelous, US$13.9 million), Wifredo Lam (Ogue Orisa, US$11.6 million) and Fernando Botero (Horse, US$5.2 million). A record tells you the most one buyer has paid for one work. It is not a measure of an artist's market as a whole, as our piece on single record sales explains.

Elsewhere this autumn

In London on 14 October, Christie's two evening sales made £218.6 million, including fees, according to Apollo. The top lot was another Kandinsky, Das bunte Leben (1907), at £31,560,000 with fees. Working back from Christie's London rates gives a hammer price of exactly £27,000,000, which we show as our calculation on Kandinsky's profile. Mondrian's Composition III (1920) made £25,235,000 and Francis Bacon's Figure in Movement (1978) £17,185,000, as reported by London Art Walk. The next day Phillips sold all 20 lots in its London evening sale for £14,836,750, led by Richter's Mathis (1983) at £5,839,000, just under its £6 million low estimate, according to its own results. Sotheby's London contemporary evening sale on 15 October made £45.9 million with fees.

In Hong Kong, the autumn sales at Sotheby's, Christie's and Phillips at the end of September passed HK$2 billion together, the South China Morning Post reported, with HK$956.5 million at Christie's and HK$956 million at Sotheby's.

What these prices can and cannot tell you

They show what one buyer paid for one work on one evening, often with a guarantee behind it. They do not show what a different work by the same artist would make, and a week of records is not a trend. Several of the highest prices were for works with museum histories and decades in one family's hands, which few other works can match. Unique works and editions are kept apart throughout this site, and none of the lots above is an edition except the Giacometti bronze, which belongs to a small cast. Nothing here is investment advice.
